Standard: 1.P.AC.3.d
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Writing, Comprehension
Competency: Use and understand multimodal texts that combine different genres, text features, and craft techniques to influence audiences and achieve specific purposes.
Official text: Consume and produce multimodal texts, integrating a variety of genres, text features, and craft techniques to influence target audiences and achieve specific purposes. (I/C)
Skills:
- Consume multimodal texts that integrate various genres, text features, and craft techniques.
- Produce multimodal texts that combine genres, text features, and craft techniques to influence target audiences and achieve specific purposes.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify different genres within multimodal texts.
- Recognize and describe various text features in multimodal texts.
- Explain how craft techniques affect the audience and purpose of a text.
- Create multimodal texts that combine genres, text features, and craft techniques to influence a target audience.
- Use multimodal elements to achieve a specific purpose in communication.
Pedagogy terms / keywords: multimodal texts, genres, text features, craft techniques, audience, purpose
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify genres, text features, and craft techniques in multimodal texts.
- written_production: Produce multimodal texts that integrate genres, text features, and craft techniques to influence audiences and purposes.
- procedural_application: Use knowledge of text design to create multimodal texts for specific audiences and purposes.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how different genres, text features, and craft techniques influence the audience and purpose of multimodal texts.
- comprehension_response: Respond to multimodal texts by discussing how their design affects audience and purpose.

Standard: 1.P.EICC.3.e
Domain primary: Comprehension
Competency: Make and keep track of predictions about what will happen next in a text.
Official text: Make and track predictions about the events and information likely to come next. (I)
Skills:
- Make predictions about events or information likely to come next in a text.
- Track those predictions as reading progresses.
Observable behaviors:
- State what they think will happen next in a story or text.
- Explain why they think a certain event or information will come next.
- Recall previous predictions and compare them to what actually happens as they read.
Pedagogy terms / keywords: predictions, comprehension strategies, monitoring understanding
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Recognize when a text invites making predictions about upcoming events or information.
- oral_production: Verbally express predictions about what will happen next in a text.
- matching_sorting_sequencing: Track the sequence of events and update predictions accordingly.
- procedural_application: Apply the strategy of making and revising predictions while reading.
- representation_modeling: Model making predictions about text events before and during reading.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain the reasoning behind predictions about upcoming text content.
- comprehension_response: Respond to texts by making and tracking predictions about future events or information.

Standard: 1.P.AC.3.c
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing
Competency: Use what you know about different modes and genres to understand how ideas and information are organized in texts.
Official text: Apply knowledge of how mode and genre impact how ideas and information are structured and arranged in texts. (I/C)
Skills:
- Apply knowledge of how mode impacts the structure of ideas and information in texts.
- Apply knowledge of how genre impacts the structure of ideas and information in texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify how the structure of a text changes depending on its mode (e.g., visual, digital, print).
- Recognize how the genre of a text influences the way ideas and information are arranged.
- Explain how the organization of a text helps the audience understand its purpose.
Pedagogy terms / keywords: mode, genre, text structure, organization, audience, purpose
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Recognize how mode and genre affect text structure.
- matching_sorting_sequencing: Sort or sequence examples of texts by mode or genre to show differences in structure.
- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of mode and genre to interpret text organization.
- representation_modeling: Model how ideas and information are arranged differently in various modes and genres.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how mode and genre impact the structure and arrangement of ideas in texts.
- comprehension_response: Respond to texts by describing how their mode and genre shape the organization of ideas and information.

Standard: 1.P.ST.2.b
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing
Competency: Use what you know about the author, audience, and context to identify and express a clear point of view or unique perspective when reading or creating texts.
Official text: Draw from knowledge of author, audience, and context to discern and establish a clear point of view or unique perspective when interpreting and constructing texts. (I/C)
Skills:
- Draw from knowledge of the author to understand texts.
- Draw from knowledge of the audience to understand texts.
- Draw from knowledge of the context to understand texts.
- Use this knowledge to discern a clear point of view or unique perspective when interpreting texts.
- Use this knowledge to establish a clear point of view or unique perspective when constructing texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Explain who the author is writing for and why.
- Identify the context of a text and how it influences the message.
- State a clear point of view or perspective about a text.
- Create a text that shows a unique perspective based on understanding the author, audience, and context.
Pedagogy terms / keywords: author, audience, context, point of view, perspective, interpret, construct
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Recognize the author, audience, and context in texts.
- oral_production: Express a clear point of view or perspective orally when discussing texts.
- written_production: Write texts that show a clear point of view or unique perspective based on author, audience, and context.
- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of author, audience, and context to interpret and create texts with a clear perspective.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how author, audience, and context influence the point of view or perspective in a text.
- comprehension_response: Interpret texts by identifying the author's purpose and perspective based on context and audience.

Standard: 1.P.AC.2.d
Domain primary: Writing
Domain secondary: Language
Competency: Organize texts using specific formats, structures, patterns, and features to influence the audience, make the text easier to understand, and support the text's purpose.
Official text: Organize texts by incorporating specific formats, structures, patterns, and features to influence the audience, facilitate accessibility, and support the text’s purpose. (I/C)

- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of text formats and features to organize writing effectively for the audience and purpose.
- representation_modeling: Model organizing texts with specific structures and features to influence the audience and support purpose.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how chosen text formats, structures, patterns, and features help influence the audience and support the text's purpose.

- reasoning_explanation: Explain how author, audience, and context influence the purpose of a text and its effectiveness.
- comprehension_response: Interpret texts by discerning purpose and evaluate texts based on how well they achieve that purpose.

- reasoning_explanation: Explain how specific features of a text affect its meaning, tone, style, purpose, and audience.
- comprehension_response: Respond to texts by discussing how their features influence meaning, tone, style, purpose, and audience.

Standard: 1.P.ST.2.c
Domain primary: Writing
Domain secondary: Comprehension, Language
Competency: Use understanding of how authors think about context and audience to choose important information, accessible text design, effective words and language, and impactful craft techniques when creating or interpreting texts.
Official text: Draw from knowledge of how authors consider context and audience to determine which information and ideas to highlight, which text design is most accessible, which word choices and language structures are most effective, and which craft techniques are most impactful. (I/C)
Skills:
- Draw from knowledge of how authors consider context and audience to determine which information and ideas to highlight.
- Determine which text design is most accessible for the intended audience.
- Decide which word choices and language structures are most effective for the audience and purpose.
- Identify which craft techniques are most impactful in the text.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify which information and ideas an author highlights based on context and audience.
- Recognize text designs that make information easier to understand for the intended audience.
- Notice word choices and language structures that suit the audience and purpose.
- Observe craft techniques authors use to make their texts more effective.
Pedagogy terms / keywords: author's purpose, audience, context, text design, word choice, language structures, craft techniques
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Recognize how authors select information and design texts for their audience and context.
- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of audience and context to determine effective information, text design, word choice, language, and craft techniques.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how authors consider context and audience to make choices about information, text design, language, and craft techniques.
- comprehension_response: Respond to texts by identifying how author choices reflect audience and context considerations.

Standard: 1.T.T.2.d

Competency: Use expository writing techniques to introduce a topic, provide facts about the topic, and give a sense of closure in writing.

- reasoning_explanation: Explain how the introduction, facts, and closure help shape understanding of the topic.
- comprehension_response: Respond to questions about the purpose of introductions, facts, and closure in expository texts.
